newsitem.title: UK: Ldn gold comes off lows but downside still beckons.
newsitem.headline: Ldn gold comes off lows but downside still beckons.

text.p: Gold bounced gently on Tuesday but the upside was probably limited after prices tumbled to 12-year lows last week, dealers said.
"There has been some fund short covering in London this morning which was followed through in New York in the afternoon," a dealer said of gold.
Gold was fixed at $320.80 an ounce, up from $317.60 in the morning and $318.00 on Monday afternoon.
But resistance was emerging around $322.00, and market sentiment was still overwhelmingly bearish, dealers said.
Analysts have pegged $300 and lower as probable targets in the medium term.
The gold price has been under pressure all year from the threat of central banks selling gold from their reserves.
It finally cracked last Thursday when the Reserve Bank of Australia announced it had sold 167 tonnes of gold from reserves over the past six months.
Gold's woes have infected the other precious metals, particularly silver, which tumbled to near four-year lows in New York late on Monday.
At midday silver fixed at $4.25, the lowest fix since November 3, 1993 and down more than 20 cents from Monday's fixing.
Silver later followed gold up off its lows and was last indicated at $4.32/$4.34, down 12 cents from Monday's London close.
But it remains vulnerable to falls to the psychological $4.00 level and beyond, analysts said.
"The support level at 434 cents has gone and silver could technically be heading for the 1991 low of 352 cents," said analyst Fran Skelley at Credit Suisse First Boston.
Dealers said good levels of buying of silver from end users which had helped support prices earlier this year had dried up over the past couple of days.
"There has also been some selling from Middle East interests but silver is not as heavily sold as gold yet," a dealer said.
The platinum group metals (PGMs) ticked lower in anticipation of the resumption of long-delayed Russian exports, awaited on July 10, dealer said.
Platinum was easier at $404.00/$407.00, down $6.50, while palladium was $7.70 lower at $174.00/$178.00.
